name: Tucana
description: The Toucan is a southern constellation introduced in the late 16th century by Dutch navigators. Although faint by stellar standards, it contains two of the most spectacular deep-sky objects visible from Earth — the globular cluster 47 Tucanae and the Small Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way visible to the naked eye.
funFact: 47 Tucanae and the Small Magellanic Cloud appear close together in the sky but are at vastly different distances — the cluster is 16,700 light-years away while the SMC is 200,000 light-years distant. They are purely a line-of-sight coincidence, but together they make Tucana one of the most rewarding patches of sky for a small telescope.
